deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this folio. The page is a printed antiquarian bookseller's catalogue. Its running head reads 'Naturwissenschaft und Physik', page 11. It lists natural-history and physics books alphabetically from Pfaff to Schaeffer, giving author, short title, format, place and year, binding, original price in parentheses and sale price in Thaler and Silbergroschen. It continues the catalogue on the previous page (p. 10, Mayer to Orphal) and the next page (p. 12, Schaeffer to Smith). There are no derivations, formulas, marginalia or handwritten annotations visible. The only numbers are prices, publication years (often abbreviated by dropping the leading 1, e.g. '853' = 1853), formats (8 = octavo, 4 = quarto, Fol = folio) and plate counts. The latest years on the page and its neighbours (858 on this page, 860 and 862 on the next) suggest the catalogue was printed c. 1862 or later. That is after the nominal 1853 bundle date, but within Riemann's lifetime. The sheet was presumably kept among his papers as scrap or as reading matter. Nothing on it can be reconstructed as a mathematical derivation.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed bookseller's catalogue of natural-science books with no mathematical content and no visible annotations by Riemann. Its only historical interest is as evidence of the kind of scrap paper or catalogues preserved in the bundle.
transcription_corrections: The document is printed (Fraktur and Antiqua type), not a manuscript. The currency symbol rendered 'ℛ' is the Thaler sign; the previous page renders the same sign as 'Thlr.[?]'.
'Pfeiffer ... Leipzig 807': the print appears to read 807, but Pfeiffer's Monographia Heliceorum viventium appeared in 1847. This is likely a catalogue misprint or a misreading of 847.
'Arraneologie' faithfully reproduces the printed spelling; the standard title is 'Araneologie'.
'Prießley' is the catalogue's spelling of Priestley.
'Ritter, L., W.' refers to Johann Wilhelm Ritter; the initial printed as 'L.' is probably 'J.' in Fraktur.
'Richtern, L. F., phisical. Tract. v. d. rar. Conzenille' matches the print.
'Cum. 8. planch. col.' (Ratzeburg) likely reads 'Cum 8 planch. col.' (with 8 coloured plates).
